subject: FinWise load test: performance targets & customer-led window
messages:
From: Ellie Chambers <ellie.chambers@finwise.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@finwise.com
Date: 2026-04-08T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: FinWise load test: performance targets & customer-led window

Thanks again for the call this morning — good alignment from our side. To recap / next steps from FinWise: we want to run a customer-led load test against the Redwood inference endpoint next week to validate latency and concurrency at scale before we move forward with the Dedicated capacity PO.

Key targets (what we'll validate):
- P95 latency goal: <= 300ms for short (<= 128 tokens) generation requests
- Sustained throughput target: ~250 req/s across the pool (peak bursts up to ~400 req/s)
- Concurrency: ~200 concurrent connections
- Streaming: we will test both non-streaming and streaming endpoints (streaming support and keepalive behavior important)

What we need from Redwood:
1) A test account / API key with rate limits disabled for the window (or elevated for the test)
2) IP allowlist / static egress IPs for our firewall team
3) Example k6 or Locust script to mirror our ramp profile (we can adapt)
4) Preferred windows — we prefer 04/14 or 04/15 02:00–06:00 UTC for a full run (we can do a shorter smoke the day before)

Attachments: I'll attach our internal ramp profile if useful (ops@finwise.com included). Let me know if the p95 target is realistic and whether there are any model variants or quantized builds we should use for the test.

Thanks,
Ellie
Ellie Chambers
Head of Platform Reliability, FinWise
ellie.chambers@finwise.com

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>

Cc: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: FinWise load test: performance targets & customer-led window

Appreciate the clear list — that's very helpful. Short answers up front: yes, we can support a customer-led run; the p95 <=300ms for short payloads is achievable on the recommended model/stack with the right routing and cache warm-up. A few clarifying Qs before we lock the window: 

- Which model variant do you want us to test against? (we recommend 'rw-infer-small-v2-quant' for cost and latency, but can run 'rw-infer-medium' if you want headroom)
- Is the payload per request ~<=128 tokens (prompt+expected generation) or do you have a mix?
- For streaming tests: do you plan to open 200 persistent streaming connections or use short-lived streaming sessions?

What we'll provide: 
- Test API key scoped to the FinWise test project (will provide creds in a secure file)
- Static IP ranges to allowlist (we'll provide 3 egress IPs and can also coordinate through our SRE if you need more)
- Example k6 script — attaching a starter k6 script (finwise-k6-script.js) you can drop into your run.
- We'll also run a 15-minute smoke test the day prior to validate certs and allowlist.

Neha/Rishi — can you confirm recommended ramp profile and any caveats for streaming/pinned connections? Also flag any model fallback behavior (e.g., automatic fallback to quantized variant) that could affect latency numbers.

I'll pencil the 04/14 02:00–06:00 UTC window pending your firewall confirmation.

Thanks,
Logan

logan_wright@redwood.ai
From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-04-08T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FinWise load test: performance targets & customer-led window

Thanks — technical notes from infra/SE: 

Ramp & concurrency recommendations:
- Start with a 10-minute warm-up at 25% of target (ramp from 60 -> 250 req/s over 10m)
- Steady-state for 60 minutes at target (~250 req/s) then 10m ramp to peak bursts (400 req/s) for 15m
- Concurrency target: 200 concurrent connections for non-streaming; for streaming, treat concurrent sessions as long-lived sockets — cap to 150 long-lived streaming connections to avoid socket exhaustion on the client side

Streaming specifics:
- When testing streaming responses, ensure your k6/Locust uses HTTP/1.1 chunked responses or HTTP/2 with flow control. We return data in small chunks; client-side buffer flush behavior affects perceived latency.
- Keepalive: enable connection reuse and set a 60s keepalive so KV cache can be leveraged across requests.

Model selection / fallback:
- Use rw-infer-small-v2-quant for primary runs (we've validated p95 ~220–280ms at 250 req/s with warmed caches)
- Automatic fallback to rw-infer-small-v2 (non-quant) is possible if instance capacity constrained — that will increase p95 (expect +50–120ms)

IP allowlist & test accounts:
- We'll provide three public egress IPs: 34.201.77.12, 34.201.77.13, 34.201.77.14 (please confirm with your firewall team)
- Test API key: will create scoped key and share via secure vault link; it will be valid only for the window

Attachments: included a starter k6 script (finwise-k6-script.js) that implements the ramp described above.

Let us know if you want us to run a parallel pass from our side for cross-checking results — we can schedule that in a separate window.

-Neha
